newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse chief sees more foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse chief sees more foreign investment.

text.p: Foreign portfolio investors are waiting in the wings to invest in the Nigerian stock market, a senior official of the Nigerian stock exchange (NSE) said on Tuesday.

"We have a lot of foreign investors hanging at the border," Henry Ogirri, deputy director general of the exchange said at the last day of trading in 1996. "Whether the foreign investors will come in or not depends on our attitude."
They would be watching out for professionalism and integrity among operators, Ogirri added.
He said the performance of the market in 1996 was impressive but more challenges awaited it in the new year.
According to him, a lot was already being done to improve trading in the new year.
Part of this would be commissioning of a computerised delivery and settlement system in the first quarter of 1997 to improve efficiency in the market.
The military government in February blamed the exchange for failing to internationalise the market and attract foreign investment.
In April the government set up a panel to suggest ways of reforming the market. Its recommendations are expected to be made public in the the 1997 budget.
But Ogirri said the exchange was already implementing many of the suggestions that could be in the panel's white paper.
Early in the year, it introduced a more liberal pricing policy, freeing share prices to move by a maximum five percent daily instead of the former maximum 20 kobo.
It also abolished a restrictive practice of allotting shares brought to the trading floor to several dealers rather than to the house that sourced them, boosting volumes.
The NSE further deregulated the market in September when it reduced fees charged investors buying or selling shares.
A controversial half percent commission levied on traders came into effect on December 1 after the dealers threatened to disrupt trading when it was first imposed in October.
At the end of trading on Tuesday, the market capitalisation for equities was 279 billion naira compared to 171 billion naira this time last year. ($1=80 naira)
